page.layout: Running head across the top of the text block: "Lib. II." and "Scutum Regium." on one line. One text column, full width, with a narrow right margin holding three notes (p, q, r) beside the text. Page number 103 at top right, above the margin. Signature "H 4" and catchword "Sed" at the foot of the column.

main_text.l: Fœlix: cùm alioquin, etiam ex proprie-
pellare potuissent: nam Cicero ait; quare

l.i: suo iure noster ille Ennius sanctos appellat
Poetas, quod quasi Deorum dono atque mu-

main_text.l: nere, nobis commendati esse videantur. Si
igitur quod à Deo datum creditur, san-
ctum dicitur; cùm constet ex Christia-
malos à Deo dari in ultionem peccato-
gem in furore meo,& {r}qui regnare facit ho-
ne utique potuit illos nominare sanctiss-
igitur ipse Deus sanctum fecit homo ne
legitimè fieri posse, tuipse (ut in seque-
ntibus apparebit) obnixè Baroni cotedis. Sed

page.notes: Margin notes: "p Tom.2. pag.546." at top right; "q Osee 13." (printed "Ofee 13"[?]) and "r Iob.27." beside the text at the marks {q} and {r}. The mark {p} in the text is taken as the letter preceding "Cæsar Baronius"[?]. The first Greek word "Ἀποστολος" is badly printed and uncertain; the printed form appears to mix Greek and Latin letters. "Hastenus" is printed with a long-s form and may be "Hactenus"[?]. The word "nalibus" at the start is a fragment continuing from the previous page. The brackets "[Sic" and "Baronius.]" are as printed.
